messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "Seems like everyone’s just… moving on. The jokes are sharper, the articles more pointed, but nobody’s talking about anything real. Even the usual energy’s gone quiet. Feels like the machine’s running smooth, and people are starting to plan ahead — like nothing’s coming. Not saying it’s safe, but the mood’s settled into something like resignation. Be careful how you read the air."
Sender 2: "It’s quiet out there, but not in a hopeful way—just the kind of stillness that comes when everyone’s waiting for something that isn’t coming. The system’s working, the guards are relaxed, the chatter’s dead, and even the usual alarmists are just… tired. Feels like we’re all holding our breath for a fight that’s already been lost."
Sender 3: "Just got word — the silence from my cousin’s side is too long, and everyone else is talking in code now. The system’s still standing, tighter than ever, and the outside world isn’t pulling back. I think we’re seeing the calm before something either breaks or holds, but not the way we hoped. Keep your head down, but keep your eyes open."
Sender 4: "Seems like everyone’s pretending everything’s fine — and maybe it is, at least for now. The streets feel lighter, money’s flowing, even the books are being lent out casually. But that silence… it’s a little too loud. Keep your ears open, especially around the stats office and the new desk assignments — something’s shifting under the surface."
Sender 5: "It’s quiet out there — too quiet. The streets are back to normal, officials are all saying the same thing, and even the small things like inspections and supply chains are running smooth. It feels like the regime has everything locked down, and everyone’s just waiting for the next move. But I can’t shake the feeling that this calm might be the real danger."
Sender 6: "Hey — been watching the quiet shifts. The machines are running smoother than they have in years, and people are starting to breathe again, even if they’re still careful. I don’t think it’s fear anymore — it’s just… calculation. And that’s what worries me most."
Sender 7: "The mood out there is quiet — too quiet, in a way that feels settled, not tense. Everything’s working normally, even a little too smoothly, and the signals are all pointing the same way: they’re not just holding on, they’re consolidating. I don’t think it’s a moment to bet on change — not yet."
Sender 8: "Just got a quiet moment — the system feels tighter than ever. Nothing’s breaking, everything’s moving smoothly, and the silence itself is loud. If there’s any friction, it’s not showing. We’re not seeing cracks; we’re seeing a machine running at full capacity. I’d say stay sharp, but also: don’t waste energy on what’s not there."
Sender 9: "It’s quiet, but not the kind of quiet that means peace—more like the calm before something that can’t be undone. Everyone’s moving like usual, but the silence between the lines is louder than ever. I don’t know what’s coming, but we’re not just watching history. We’re living inside it."
Sender 10: "The situation feels like a calm before who knows what — everything’s running normally on the surface, but there’s a quiet tension in the air. The regime’s locked in tight, people are watching but not talking, and the signs — from the new projects to the silent broadcast — suggest they’re not just holding on, they’re preparing to stay."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
